key_insight: QSTAR shows that quantum heads are most valuable as selective fallback routes for uncertain samples, not as full replacements for strong classical classifiers.
engineering_relevance: For hybrid quantum-classical systems, adaptive routing can improve end-to-end performance by reserving quantum computation for low-confidence cases where it adds the most value.
method: Compare manual QTL heads, KetGPT-searched quantum heads, and parameter-matched classical baselines
Route high-confidence predictions classically and send low-confidence samples to a fallback branch
evidence_signal: Across a common split and training setup, the best KetGPT head reached 78.5% accuracy, and the adaptive KetGPT-QTL system achieved 80.9% accuracy and 0.807 F1-score, outperforming the adaptive classical baseline.
watch_item: The gains depend on confidence-threshold routing and a specific frozen-backbone setup, so results may not transfer directly to other datasets, models, or quantum hardware constraints.
paper_title: QSTAR: Quantum Selective Transfer with Adaptive Routing
